new_items.title: Attribute core filesystem work and select one systemic optimization
new_items.review_state: source-proven repeated work; latency gain unmeasured
new_items.problem: Rich full-engine checks eagerly fetch metadata without a size limit, independently walk overlapping scopes, and scan all scopes per uncached directory. Existing static fast-path indexes and prepared reuse already exist. No current wall-time fraction or causal speedup is established.
acceptance_criteria: Profile ordinary public check with a source/binary/policy-bound rich repository and controlled wide-tree case; count stat-family calls, directory enumerations, reads/bytes, allocations or peak RSS, CPU and wall time by consumer.
First discriminate no-size-policy eager metadata; then attribute identical-scope test/lifecycle enumeration. Preserve a naming-only negative control and full result/exit equivalence.
Produce one smallest supported keep/defer decision; do not implement a shared inventory, index rewrite, daemon, new entrypoint or parallel traversal merely because source work is repeated.

For any later performance candidate, use uninstrumented balanced same-host before/after public-command samples, exact quiet comparison, existing keep/stop criteria, accepted-fixture spillover and unchanged no-slower/native/warm gates.

Keep literal/glob scope indexing conditional on measured dominance. Incremental eligibility expansion additionally requires NU13 coverage resolution and deletion/rename/provider/config invalidation proof; source review alone proves no gain.
new_items.next_action: Run one bounded full-engine filesystem-I/O attribution spike on an idle admitted host.
new_items.priority_rationale: Explicit user focus on systemic filesystem performance; one investigation, not four speculative implementation cards.
